comments.body: @benvanik, @laurenzo, or @silvasean can you confirm the intended behavior here? I think the tie_shape should just change its return type and pass through and then later we should drop it. I tried dropping it right away, but some patterns during this conversion look for a tie shape to determine some argument's shape so we have to leave it around until the conversion is done.

Can't comment on this specific issues, but that func looks like it has a verifier error: `return %1 : tensor<?xi32>` but the function return type is `!hal.buffer`, so it seems like something has gone wrong already.

Note that if the `return` op is fixed to return !hal.buffer to be consistent with the function, then this specific tie_shape verifier error goes away.

Yeah that's basically the same error. If the correct behavior is to have
the tie_shape apply to a buffer then it would return a buffer and go
through to make the return value a buffer as well

issue.title: Cannot lower tie_shape outside of stream fragment

issue.body:
Currently all tie_shape ops are being forced into streams: https://github.com/google/iree/blob/6faf80410fb381556f07d906c235b70ce344c770/iree/compiler/Dialect/Flow/Transforms/FormStreams.cpp#L47-L49

This has the side-effect of creating empty streams that perform no real work:
```mlir
    %cmd = hal.command_buffer.create %dev, "OneShot", "Transfer|Dispatch" : !hal.command_buffer
    hal.command_buffer.begin %cmd
    hal.command_buffer.end %cmd
    hal.ex.submit_and_wait %dev, %cmd
```

We should instead be looking for ops that *must* be in streams (StreamableOpInterface::isStreamOnly) and then trying to gather/possibly duplicate ops that are stream-compatible (StreamableOpInterface::isUsableInStream). We can also reorder ops to pull work above/below non-streamable ops instead of just splitting like we are now.

A better algorithm for constructing stream fragments will help #1161.
